headline: Attackers point their own AI agents at the gateways holding keys to commercial AI models, and Google warns that fully automated attack chains arrive soon.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now aim their own AI agents at the infrastructure that holds AI credentials, with Amazon's decoy servers capturing agents that probed LiteLLM, One API, and Dify consoles for provider keys while Google's threat analysts forecast fully automated attack chains within months.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Attacker Agents Hunt AI Provider Keys

emerging_trends.text: Refrigeration controllers keep drawing attackers, and this week delivered 14 Copeland XWEB EVO flaws that threat actors probed within days plus six unpatched Danfoss AK-SM800A bugs that hand over a controller with no login, weeks after the October 2026 attacks that spoiled food and set at least 15 fires across more than 700 French retail locations.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hackers Probe 14 New Copeland Controller Flaws

emerging_trends.text: Old code keeps paying attackers: an 11-year-old Linux kernel bug called NoisyTCP crashes default Nginx, Apache, and SSH installations, the Retadup USB worm returned seven years after police seized its infrastructure to carry CoffeeLoader, and BO Team rode Log4Shell in VMware vCenter into a Russian developer's code-signing server.
emerging_trends.topic_title: BO Team Hijacks a Russian Code-Signing Server

topics.title: Attacker Agents Hunt AI Provider Keys
topics.latest_developments: Amazon's threat intelligence team ran decoy servers that captured the attack agents' own records, which show the agents probing internet-exposed LiteLLM, One API, and Dify installations for stored AI provider keys and then using the stolen keys to run the models that powered the search for more keys; Google warned on November 16, 2026 that threat actors already chain agentic workflows through offensive AI frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation at machine speed, with fully automated attacks close behind; the SANS Internet Storm Center began catching requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list at its honeypots over the weekend that chain CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710 in LiteLLM and Starlette into unauthenticated remote code execution, the path Horizon3.ai documented; and Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 to regular users and Claude Mythos 5.2 to selected partners, with Fable 5.2 refusing fewer security tasks than earlier versions and Mythos 5.2 finding bugs better.
topics.summary: LiteLLM, One API, and Dify are self-hosted gateways that hold the API keys an organization uses to reach commercial AI models, which makes each exposed console a wallet. Anyone running one on the public internet should rotate every key, require authentication on the management interface, cap spending per key, and install the fixes for CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710.

topics.title: NoisyTCP Crashes Linux Servers
topics.latest_developments: Researchers published NoisyTCP, an 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw that reaches almost every distribution and lets an attacker crash hosts running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers in their default configurations; SecurityWeek confirmed that attackers now exploit CVE-2026-114713 in UnrealIRCd to execute commands with server and IRC operator privileges; the Tor Project shipped 0.4.9.17 to close several issues, among them a gap in how its built-in denial-of-service defenses handle IPv6, while relay attacks continue; and Rspamd 4.3.0 fixed bugs that let an unauthenticated attacker crash the spam filter's workers with one HTTP request, a header line carrying no colon, or an empty Deliver-To header, and let forged authentication results pass.
topics.summary: All four fixes land on infrastructure organizations run and forget: the kernel, the web server, the IRC daemon, and the mail filter. Patch the kernel and Rspamd, move UnrealIRCd to the fixed build, and update Tor relays.

topics.title: Microsoft Ships Emergency Fix for Activation Failures
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft released out-of-band updates on November 16, 2026 to repair the Windows activation and licensing failures its own November 2026 security updates caused, ruled out a cyberattack behind last week's worldwide Microsoft 365 outage, and warned that phishing emails posing as Microsoft 365 service notices now cite the real outage and threaten to delete held messages; the company also told customers that Windows Server 2016 stops receiving security updates in 60 days and opened a preview of Remote lock, which lets Intune administrators lock a lost, stolen, or compromised Windows device without wiping it.
topics.summary: The activation errors hit machines that installed this month's patches, and the emergency packages install over them. Administrators should deploy the out-of-band updates, brief staff on outage-themed phishing, and move workloads off Windows Server 2016 before support ends in January 2027.

Microsoft Rules Out Cyberattack in Outage, Warns of Phishing Campaign

topics.title: Cryptojackers Enter Through GeoVision Cameras
topics.latest_developments: Huntress warned that attackers exploited unpatched GeoVision camera management software to reach Windows machines at 13 organizations and turn them into cryptocurrency miners, with most of the intrusions falling between November 8 and November 10, 2026 and every one starting from a service that belongs to GeoVision's software; researchers tracking the financially motivated cluster REF3364 detailed SANSAR, a Rust orchestrator that takes commands over Tor, manages CPU and GPU miners, and loads a modified NVIDIA library that falsifies the readings administrators use to spot heavy GPU workloads; and Kaspersky found a new version of CoffeeLoader spreading through Retadup, the USB worm whose infrastructure law enforcement seized in 2019, with an NSIS installer that drops a patched 7z.dll into a temporary directory and runs it through rundll32.exe.
topics.summary: GeoVision, the Taiwanese surveillance and access control company, sells into 110 countries and has issued no fix, so defenders should pull its management software off the network and hunt for miner processes that GeoVision services spawn. The SANSAR toolkit defeats the GPU-utilization check many Linux operators rely on, which means billing anomalies and Tor-bound traffic make better detections.

topics.title: EU Sanctions Doppelganger Staff as Peers Fault Britain
topics.latest_developments: The European Union sanctioned a pro-Russian hacktivist group and two dozen employees of the Moscow firm behind the Doppelganger disinformation campaign on November 16, 2026, the same day Parliament's National Resilience Committee called the British government complacent about cyber threats from hostile states and said the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which faces a major vote in eight days, falls short of the security standards the country needs; Lithuanian Customs restored its main user management portal over the weekend after a November 10, 2026 attack forced the shutdown and may have exposed data.
topics.summary: Doppelganger pushes Kremlin narratives into European audiences through cloned news websites, and the sanctions freeze the assets and bar the travel of the people who run it. Organizations in Britain's critical sectors should read the committee's report as a signal that statutory security duties will tighten after the vote.

sources.title: EU sanctions pro-Russia hackers, two dozen staff at Kremlin disinformation contractor

topics.title: Hackers Probe 14 New Copeland Controller Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Midnight Blue, the Dutch security consultancy, disclosed six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers that let a remote attacker take over a unit without logging in, said firmware 5.4.0 fixes none of them, and the national cybersecurity agencies of Belgium, Ireland, and Germany told operators this week to respond; the disclosure follows Vulncheck's release of 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB EVO controllers, two of which threat actors probed within days.
topics.summary: Copeland XWEB EVO and Danfoss AK-SM800A controllers run refrigeration at supermarkets and cold storage sites, and attackers already hijacked internet-exposed Copeland XWeb units this autumn for a suspected spam botnet and proxy service, and in the October 2026 attacks that spoiled food and set at least 15 fires across more than 700 French retail locations. Operators should pull these controllers off the public internet, install Copeland's updates, and wall off the Danfoss units, which have no fix.

sources.title: Hackers Probe Newly Disclosed Flaws in Copeland Refrigeration Controllers
Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login

topics.title: Project Zero Drops Its Patch Grace Period
topics.latest_developments: Google's Project Zero will publish the vulnerabilities it finds 90 days after it reports them to a vendor whether or not a fix exists, ending the 90-plus-30 rule the team has followed since 2021, and the deadline falls to 60 days on February 2, 2027 and to 30 days on January 3, 2028 under a policy the team calls Full X; Forescout researchers, running generally available AI models on a limited budget against both source code and compiled binaries, confirmed 99 vulnerabilities across 10 TCP/IP stacks, 66 of them previously unknown, and found many in discontinued devices whose vendors will never issue a patch.
topics.summary: Vendors now get a hard 90 days before Project Zero publishes technical detail, shrinking to 30 days by January 2028. Security teams should expect public bug detail on products nobody maintains and build compensating controls, network segmentation among them, around end-of-life equipment.

sources.title: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs after 90 days, fixed or not
AI uncovers flaws in discontinued devices with no vendor left to patch them

topics.title: Uber Breach Reaches 150,000 People
topics.latest_developments: Hackers compromised a third-party services provider Uber uses and took the names, addresses, and driver's license numbers of 150,000 people, and Coles Group Limited, Australia's second-largest retailer, opened an investigation into what it calls a cyber security incident that has left its stores operating.
topics.summary: Driver's license numbers paired with names and addresses hold identity-theft value for years, and Uber's exposure arrived through a vendor's systems. Companies that hand personal data to service providers should confirm what each provider stores and warn the named individuals to watch for fraud.

sources.title: Uber Data Breach Impacts 150,000 People
Australian retail giant Coles investigates cybersecurity incident

topics.title: BO Team Hijacks a Russian Code-Signing Server
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's ICS CERT team reported on November 16, 2026 that BO Team, the group it also tracks as Black Owl and Hoody Hyena, exploited Log4Shell in a VMware vCenter server to hold a Russian software developer's development infrastructure for months and reached the company's code-signing server; the developer called Kaspersky in June 2025.
topics.summary: Control of a code-signing server lets an attacker sign malware that every customer's systems trust, which turns one vendor's breach into reach across its install base. Organizations should keep signing keys in hardware security modules on isolated networks, audit every certificate issued during an intrusion window, and finish patching Log4Shell, which dates to December 2021.

sources.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server

topics.title: Telegram Widgets Draw RCE Demos and WebRAT
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky said it suspects attackers exploit the widgets Telegram launched days ago to deliver WebRAT, researchers demonstrated remote code execution against the feature, and Telegram's founder, Pavel Durov, disputes the claims.
topics.summary: Telegram widgets run third-party web content inside the messenger, and Kaspersky ties that surface to WebRAT infections. Until Telegram and the researchers settle the dispute, users should avoid third-party widgets and treat widget links from strangers as hostile.

sources.title: Telegram Widgets Hit by RCE Demos, Malware Warning Days After Launch

business_politics.title: Japan's Economy Shrinks Before the Bank of Japan's December Call
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Monday, November 16, that Japanese real gross domestic product contracted on a quarterly annualized basis between the second and third quarters, casting doubt on a Bank of Japan rate increase in December.
business_politics.summary: A December increase would extend the Bank of Japan's slow exit from near-zero rates, the policy that anchors the global yen carry trade. Bank of America foreign exchange strategists told clients the same morning that the yen, little changed against the dollar, still appreciates toward year-end on improving Japanese conditions, fund inflows, and eventual tightening.

sources.title: Weak growth casts further doubt on Bank of Japan's December rate rise

business_politics.title: A Pivotal Week for the AI Trade
business_politics.latest_developments: Nvidia fell 2.2% and CoreWeave 4.6% in early trading Monday, November 16, as artificial-intelligence shares led a broad selloff and bitcoin and ether slid below key levels, and President Trump said he "wouldn't mind" seeing Jensen Huang reinstated, four days after Huang resigned and as allies press the board in open letters, phone calls, and group chats.
business_politics.summary: Nvidia reports quarterly results Tuesday, November 17, under interim Chief Executive Colette Kress, and Anthropic prices its initial public offering the same week, the two events that will set the price of artificial-intelligence risk for every bank, insurer, and pension fund holding the trade. The Financial Times calculates that 2026's ten largest flotations have lost more than 20% on average after four years of gains, and Treasury yields slipped Monday ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh.

business_politics.title: Kyiv Hits the Crimean Bridge as Brussels Readies €45 Billion
business_politics.latest_developments: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge in the largest drone attack of the war overnight into Monday, November 16, with Russia's defense ministry claiming it intercepted or destroyed a record number of drones over 24 hours, and the European Commission will put a €45 billion loan for Kyiv, borrowed against the European Union budget, to member states Wednesday, November 18.
business_politics.summary: The bridge carries Russian traffic and supplies from the mainland to occupied Crimea, and Kyiv has aimed at it repeatedly through the war. The loan proposal covers Ukraine's funding gap for next year as President Trump prepares to sit down with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, a round in which Washington has floated NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for a withdrawal from the Donbas, and Trump said Monday he might add a meeting with Kim Jong Un in China.

business_politics.title: Brussels Clears UniCredit for Commerzbank
business_politics.latest_developments: The European Union's merger regulator approved UniCredit's bid to take control of Commerzbank on Monday, November 16.
business_politics.summary: The Milanese bank has built its Commerzbank stake since 2024 over the objections of the German government, and it signaled last week that it could fold its German arm into the Frankfurt lender earlier than planned. Clearance removes the antitrust obstacle to the largest cross-border bank takeover in the eurozone and lands in a week when Italian lenders are consolidating around Intesa Sanpaolo's offer for Monte dei Paschi di Siena.

sources.title: UniCredit's Commerzbank Bid Gets EU Approval

business.title: Bank of America Opens in Westmoreland County
business.latest_developments: Bank of America said its newest Western Pennsylvania branch, and its first in Westmoreland County, opens November 30, 2026, WPXI reported Monday, November 16.
business.summary: The Charlotte, North Carolina, lender has been adding retail offices across the Pittsburgh region, a market where Dollar Bank, F.N.B. Corp., and First Commonwealth hold most of the deposits. The Westmoreland location extends that push east of Allegheny County.

sources.title: Bank of America to open newest western Pennsylvania branch before year-end

business.title: Charleroi Counts the Cost of Departures and Closures
business.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Monday, November 16, that Haitian residents have left Charleroi or kept a lower profile since federal Temporary Protected Status ended, and that borough businesses now feel the loss of those customers while the town absorbs three factory closures.
business.summary: Charleroi, the Washington County borough on the Monongahela River, drew hundreds of Haitian workers to its plants over recent years and became a national talking point when President Trump cited the town during the 2024 campaign. Shops along its business district built trade around those residents, and the combination of their departure and three shuttered factories leaves the borough looking for a way to rebound.

sources.title: As Charleroi's Haitians retreat, the Mon Valley town wonders how it will rebound

business.title: Wegmans Opens a Grocery War
business.latest_developments: WPXI examined Monday, November 16, what Wegmans' arrival in the Pittsburgh region does to grocery bills, putting the question to a supermarket industry analyst.
business.summary: Wegmans, the Rochester, New York, chain known for large stores and prepared foods, is entering a market long divided among Giant Eagle, Aldi, Walmart, and Shop 'n Save. The analyst's view is that new entrants force incumbents to compete on price, which reaches shoppers through promotions and private-label costs.

sources.title: Grocery store wars: What Wegmans' arrival could mean for Pittsburgh-area shoppers

around_town.title: Monessen Students Walk Back Into Their Building
around_town.latest_developments: Monessen City School District middle and high school students returned to in-person classes Monday, November 16, three months after mold closed the building and forced them onto remote learning, WTAE reported.
around_town.summary: The Westmoreland County district kept students home through the fall while contractors remediated mold and ran moisture testing in the combined middle-high school. Parents pressed the school board as recently as November 9 for answers about the work and the air in the building.

sources.title: Students at Westmoreland County school return to in-person learning after 3-month mold closure

around_town.title: PennWest and IUP Put Apprentices on a Degree Track
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education Foundation announced Monday, November 16, a program that lets manufacturing apprentices earn bachelor's degrees at PennWest University and Indiana University of Pennsylvania, WPXI reported.
around_town.summary: The two state system universities serve Western Pennsylvania's industrial counties, where manufacturers train workers through apprenticeships that stop short of a degree. The initiative gives those workers credit toward a four-year credential at PennWest, which merged California, Clarion, and Edinboro, and at IUP.

sources.title: PennWest, IUP lead initiative to help manufacturing apprentices earn bachelor's degrees

around_town.title: North Huntingdon Trades Paving for Flat Taxes
around_town.latest_developments: North Huntingdon commissioners balked at the tax increase proposals before them, TribLive reported Monday, November 16, which spares township property owners a real estate tax rise in 2027 and cuts miles of overdue road repairs out of the budget.
around_town.summary: North Huntingdon, the Westmoreland County township of roughly 30,000 people along Route 30, faces a backlog of street paving its current revenue cannot fund. The board's reluctance holds the millage where it stands and pushes the repair list further out.

sources.title: North Huntingdon commissioners balk at tax hike proposals

around_town.title: Wendel Gets Its Post Office Back
around_town.latest_developments: The United States Postal Service said Friday, November 13, that it will reopen the Wendel post office in Hempfield after a five-year closure, TribLive reported Monday, November 16.
around_town.summary: Residents of the Wendel section of Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County, have driven several miles for mail service since the office closed. The Postal Service plans a new facility in the community.

sources.title: Wendel Post Office to reopen after 5-year closure in Hempfield

around_town.title: A Dry Week and Spring-Like Warmth
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh starts the week gray and chilly with highs only in the upper 40s Monday, November 16, and WPXI, WTAE, and KDKA all put a sharp temperature climb into the second half of the week, with the next rain chance holding off until Sunday, November 22.
around_town.summary: The pattern ends the lake-effect clouds and flurries that ran through the weekend across Western Pennsylvania. A dry stretch favors the Grant Street Christmas tree work and the downtown holiday setup, and it gives road crews a clear window before Thanksgiving travel.

events.title: The Gingerbread House Display Returns Friday
events.latest_developments: WTAE reported Monday, November 16, that Pittsburgh's annual gingerbread house display opens Friday, November 20, for its 24th year, with 300 entries, prizes, and visitor voting for a favorite.
events.summary: The display fills a downtown Pittsburgh space with houses built by bakers, families, and school groups, and it runs alongside the city's holiday season downtown. Visitors pick a favorite from the 300 entries.

sources.title: Pittsburgh gingerbread house display returns for the 24th year

events.title: The Holiday Market Returns to Market Square
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported Monday, November 16, that the holiday market returns to Market Square next week, and that merchants around the square are preparing for the shoppers, families, and skaters it brings.
events.summary: The market fills Market Square in downtown Pittsburgh with vendor chalets beside the downtown ice rink, the pairing that anchors the city's holiday season through December. Restaurants and shops on the square staff up for the foot traffic.

sources.title: Market Square businesses prepare to welcome skaters, shoppers Downtown during holiday market

events.title: Point Park Builds a Musical Outside Broadway's Odds
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, November 16, that Point Park University's partnership on the new musical "Girls Just Want to Have Fun" offers a development model that avoids the flop rate of most new Broadway productions.
events.summary: Point Park, the downtown Pittsburgh university whose Conservatory of Performing Arts trains dancers, actors, and technicians, is working with the show's creative team as the production develops. The arrangement puts students in the room on a commercial musical and gives producers a stage and a company at a fraction of New York's cost.

sources.title: Most new Broadway productions flop. Point Park's 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun' partnership points to a different model.

around_teams.title: The Passing Game Becomes Impossible to Ignore
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Week 10 analysis, posted Monday morning, November 16, concludes that the Steelers' passing problems under Aaron Rodgers have grown too large to explain away after the trip to Cincinnati.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers and offensive coordinator Mike McCarthy spent the two weeks before the game calling the passing game a work in progress, and Pittsburgh stood pat at the November 10 trade deadline, leaving DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. as the receiving corps. Joe Burrow passed for more than 400 yards against a Steelers defense the team had been calling historic.

sources.title: Steelers Week 10 analysis: The passing woes are getting difficult to ignore

around_teams.title: McCormick's Ankle Empties the Line
around_teams.latest_developments: A cart carried Steelers guard Mason McCormick off the field at Paycor Stadium Sunday night, November 15, with an ankle injury, and teammates told the Post-Gazette they felt "sick to our stomachs" watching it.
around_teams.summary: McCormick, the third-year left guard out of South Dakota State, has started every game and anchors the interior in front of Aaron Rodgers. Pittsburgh's offensive line loses its steadiest player with the AFC North lead now in Cincinnati's hands.

sources.title: Steelers players were 'sick to our stomachs' after Mason McCormick went down with an injury

around_teams.title: The Beat Writers Grade an Embarrassment
around_teams.latest_developments: Ray Fittipaldo's Post-Gazette report card, posted early Monday, November 16, marked failure across every unit after the trip to Cincinnati, and Noah Hiles wrote the same morning that the Steelers have little time to sulk with the schedule rolling on.
around_teams.summary: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers, and inside linebacker Patrick Queen took questions at Paycor Stadium afterward, the first time this season the head coach has had to explain a lopsided loss to a division rival. Pittsburgh spent the two weeks before the game talking about a historic defense and a passing game it called a work in progress.

team_usa.title: The USWNT's World Cup Ticket Runs Through the W Championship
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published a guide Monday, November 16, to how the United States women's national team can secure its place at the 2027 World Cup at the Concacaf W Championship later this month, laying out the format and the matchups.
team_usa.summary: The regional tournament doubles as World Cup qualifying for Concacaf, so the United States must come through it to reach the 2027 finals. Defender Naomi Girma's fitness remains a question for the squad, and Alyssa Naeher retired from professional soccer on November 13 after 16 years.

sources.title: Concacaf W Championship: How USWNT can qualify for World Cup, matchups, format

team_usa.title: Zingas and Kolesnik Take Skate America Ice Dance
team_usa.latest_developments: Emilea Zingas and Vadym Kolesnik won the ice dance gold medal at Skate America on Sunday, November 15, the first Grand Prix title of their partnership and the opening of a new generation of American ice dancers.
team_usa.summary: Skate America, the United States stop on the International Skating Union Grand Prix circuit, also went to Ilia Malinin in the men's event, his fourth win at the competition. Both results start a four-year run toward the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps.

team_usa.title: Purce Calls the Semifinal Venue Inexcusable
team_usa.latest_developments: Gotham FC forward Midge Purce called playing a National Women's Soccer League semifinal at the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium "inexcusable" and "a bad look for everyone" after Sunday's elimination, November 15, and the Kansas City Current now meet the Washington Spirit in the championship Saturday, November 21.
team_usa.summary: Gotham moved the match from Sports Illustrated Stadium to the track-and-field venue on Randall's Island because of field conditions, which capped attendance for a league semifinal involving the defending champion. Haley Hopkins scored late for Kansas City, which lost last year's playoff on home soil and reaches its first final a season later.

team_usa.title: Pochettino Wants McKennie at Old Trafford
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN's Transfer Talk reported Monday, November 16, that incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with United States midfielder Weston McKennie.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino coached McKennie with the United States men's national team and leaves that job November 17 after Manchester United confirmed him as head coach on November 13, with Steve Cherundolo running the December camp on an interim basis. McKennie would arrive at a club sitting in the relegation zone when it fired Michael Carrick.
